newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock indices end mostly up, mood cautious.
newsitem.headline: China stock indices end mostly up, mood cautious.

text.p: China's stock indices ended higher on Tuesday except the Shenzhen B index which was pushed down by profit-taking after Monday's steep gains, brokers said.

Investors' concerns over further crackdown measures also curbed market exuberance after Hong Kong's South China Morning Post reported on Tuesday that China's central bank governor Dai Xianglong had vowed to take further action to stop speculation, they said.
The Shenzhen B index shaved off 0.92 points, or 0.57 percent, to finish at 159.34 on turnover of HK$91.4 million against HK$93.2 million on Monday.
The Shanghai B index edged up 0.468 points, or 0.52 percent, to 90.513 points on volume of 21.012 million shares worth $17.181 million.
"Some impatient investors cashed in on yesterday's steep rise, fearing a repeat of recent market falls triggered by Beijing's crackdown," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
"Beijing may punish some institutions to issue a warning this time, but it will be good for the markets in the long run," an analyst at a foreign investment bank in Shenzhen said.
The South China Morning Post's report had less impact on the Shanghai market as the local institutionals were seen supporting shares with heavy index weighting even though losers outnumbered gainers.
Of 43 Shanghai B shares, 41 traded, with 15 up, seven flat and 19 down.

"Domestic institutions were seen supporting big companies, but most investor funds, especially overseas capital, remained sidelined due to uncertainty about the government's measures to cool the overheating market," said one Shanghai broker.
Shanghai Material Trading Centre was the star on speculative buying, jumping $0.011, or 6.58 percent, to $0.178 on volume of 123,000 shares.
Shanghai Dazhong Taxi followed on institutional support, up $0.120, or 6.49 percent, to $1.968 on volume of 1.6 million shares.

Pudong real estate counter Shanghai Jinqiao Export Processing Zone Development was the most actively traded on domestic buying, rising $0.028, or 3.63 percent, to $0.798 on volume of 2.1 million shares.

On the Shenzhen B share market, Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Ltd was the most actively traded stock on volume of 2.6 million shares. The share lost HK$0.03 to close at HK$6.92 on profit-taking, brokers said.
The Shenzhen A share index rose 3.38 points, or 0.72 percent, to 469.90, with turnover expanding to 9.7 billion yuan from Monday's 8.2 billion yuan.

The Shanghai A index edged up 2.449 points, or 0.18 percent, to 1,397.788 on volume of 659.9 million shares worth 9.9 billion yuan. The SSE30 blue chip index put on 6.458 points, or 0.16 percent, to 4,086.584 points.
